title: High-yield enrichment of mouse small intestine intraepithelial lymphocytes by immunomagnetic depletion of EpCAM+ cells
protocol: Sacrifice mice by carbon dioxide asphyxiation.
Douse carcasses with 70% ethanol to prevent fur contamination.
Make small dorsal incisions in the pelvis region using scissors.
Remove the pelt from the head to the base of the tail carefully tearing the skin transversely.
Turn over the mouse onto its ventral side.
Cut open the peritoneal membrane using scissors to expose the intestine.
Cut the SI below the pyloric sphincter and above the cecum using scissors.
Pull out the intestine using forceps.
Remove the mesenteric fat using another set of forceps.
Place the small intestine into a 10 cm petri dish pre-layered with 2% FBS-HBSS.
Flush out the fecal content with 2% FBS-HBSS using a 12 mL syringe with a 16G blunt needle.
Slide the small intestine onto the needle as you flush to remove fecal matter.
Transfer the small intestine to a new dish with 2% FBS-HBSS.
Repeat the flushing process to ensure all fecal content is removed.
Remove visible mesenteric fat from the SI using two curved blunt-edged forceps on a paper towel.
Cover the SI with 2% FBS-HBSS during removal of fat.
Return the fat-free SI to the petri dish for a second round of flushing.
Transfer the flushed SI into a new petri dish pre-layered with 2% FBS-HBSS.
Cut open the SI longitudinally using scissors.
Shake the SI using forceps to remove mucus and any remaining fecal content.
Transfer the cut-open SI to a new dish with 2% FBS-HBSS and repeat shaking process.
Perform visual inspection of the processed SI to confirm complete removal of fecal matter and mucus.
Slice the cut-open SI into ∼1 cm pieces.
Transfer the SI pieces into a 50 mL tube and fill up to 25 mL with 2% FBS-HBSS and shake.
Pour out the content into a new petri dish.
Using forceps, transfer the cut SI pieces into the same 50 mL tube and fill up to 25 mL with 2% FBS-HBSS and shake again.
Mix a blunt needle with the lumen of the small intestine (SI).
Flush out fecal matter from the SI.
Remove attached mesenteric fat if necessary.
Cut the SI longitudinally.
Prepare SI fragments by cutting them into approximately 1 cm pieces in solution A.
Incubate SI fragments under orbital shaking to release lymphocytes.
Pipette 25 mL of pre-warmed solution A into a 125 mL conical flask.
Pour out the entire contents of the 50 mL tube with SI pieces into a new petri dish.
Transfer the cut SI pieces from the petri dish into the conical flask containing solution A using forceps.
Shake the conical flask at 240 rpm at 37°C for 45 min in a pre-warmed orbital shaker.
Transfer the SI eluate, which will be around 25 mL, into a 50 mL tube by passing it through 70 μm cell strainers.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,500 rpm (500 × g) for 7 min at 10°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL cold PBS.
Take an 1 mL aliquot of the cell suspension and set it aside at 4°C to compare purity before and after EpCAM+ cell depletion.
Fill up the 50 mL tube with SI eluate to 25 mL with cold PBS.
Centrifuge the tube again at 1,500 rpm (500 × g) for 7 min at 10°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 10 μL of the single cell suspension from step 2f to 190 μL 0.08% trypan blue (1:20 dilution).
Take 10 μL of the cell suspension and count the cells using a hematocytometer.
Resuspend the cells in 10% FBS-HBSS at a concentration of 20 million cells/mL.
Add 15 μL/mL of 0.5 mg/mL anti-EpCAM antibody to the resuspended cells.
Incubate the cell suspension undisturbed on ice for 30 min.
Fill up the tubes up to 25 mL with 10% FBS-HBSS after incubation.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,500 rpm (500 × g) for 7 min at 10°C to remove excess antibodies.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 10% FBS-HBSS to an estimated concentration of 50 million/mL.
Take each 2 mL of goat anti-rat IgG-coated and goat anti-mouse IgG-coated BioMag magnetic beads for 100 million cells.
Transfer the beads into a 14 mL polypropylene round-bottom tube.
Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration while keeping the tubes attached to the magnet.
Resuspend the BioMag beads in 10 mL of 10% FBS-HBSS.
Place the cell suspension on the magnet for an additional 5 min.
Repeat this process one more time.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 1 mL of 10% FBS-HBSS.
Add cells from step 4d to the bead suspension.
Transfer the suspension into a 5 mL polypropylene tube.
Place the tube on the MACSmix™ tube rotator for 40 min at 4°C.
Place the tube on a magnet for 5 min after rotation.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 5 mL polypropylene tube.
Place the new tube on the magnet for another 5 min.
Remove residual magnetic beads from the cell suspension.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 14 mL tube.
Keep the supernatant on ice until further use.
Measure the volume of the supernatant to determine recovered cell numbers.
Add 10 μL of single-cell suspension to 190 μL 0.08% trypan blue.
Count cells using a hematocytometer from step 6a.
Mix magnetic beads with cells before rotation.
Rotate tubes containing cell-bead mixture.
Separate magnetic beads from cell suspension using magnet.
Take 5 million IELs and transfer into 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tubes.
Add 2 mL of cold FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,500 rpm (500×g) for 7 minutes at 10°C.
Discard supernatant from the tubes.
Stain cells with antibodies to surface markers in FACS buffer according to dilution factors indicated.
Create a master mix including all fluorescence-conjugated antibodies and anti-mouse CD16/32 blocking antibody.
Add 70 μL of the antibody master mix to each tube.
For single-color compensation tubes, add 10 μL of diluted antibody according to the staining chart.
Add 5 μL anti-mouse CD16/32 (Clone: 2.4G2) to all tubes.
Incubate tubes at 4°C for 30 min.
Add 2 mL of cold FACS buffer to each tube.
Spin down cells at 1,500 rpm (500 × g) for 7 min at 10°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells again with 2 mL cold FACS buffer.
Resuspend pellet with 200 μL cold FACS buffer.
Filter the cells into new FACS tubes through a 60 μm nylon filter.
Place the tubes on ice until flow cytometric analysis.
Collect at least 0.5 million PI-negative live-gated cells per tube.
Set flow rate to 6,000 events/second or less.
Adjust voltage settings as follows: FCS: 565, SSC: 330, FITC: 500, PE-Cy7: 630, eFluor 450: 390, Alexa Fluor 647: 460, Alexa Fluor 594: 510, APC-e780: 580, BV786: 580, PI: 375.
Use unstained compensation tubes for voltage adjustment.
Use single color-stained compensation tubes for voltage adjustment.
Analyze .FCS format flow cytometry files using FlowJo software.
Set linear scales for Forward Scatter Height (FSC-H) and Forward Scatter Width (FCS-W).
Set log scales for fluorochrome parameters.
Perform statistical analyses using GraphPad Prism 7 software.
Create figures for publication using Canvas X graphical software.
